draft.title: Linear growth and decay
card: In linear growth, the same amount is added at each step. In linear decay, the same amount is taken away at each step.
As a recurrence relation, growth is u(n+1) = u(n) + d and decay is u(n+1) = u(n) − d. The amount d stays fixed.
Simple interest is linear growth. The interest is worked out on the original amount only, so the same dollar amount is added each year.
Flat-rate depreciation is linear decay. An item loses the same dollar amount each year. Example: a $2000 laptop losing $300 a year is worth $2000 − 3 × $300 = $1100 after 3 years.
draft.remember: Linear means the same amount is added or taken away at each step.

a.q: Priya invests $1500 at 4% simple interest per year. How much interest is added each year?
a.why: Simple interest is 4% of the original $1500, which is $60 every year. The amount $62.40 is 4% of $1560, which is not how simple interest works.
a.clue: Simple interest always uses the original amount.

b.q: A van bought for $42 000 loses $6000 in value each year under flat-rate depreciation. What is its value after 4 years?
b.why: The loss is 4 × $6000 = $24 000. So the value is $42 000 − $24 000 = $18 000. The answer $24 000 is the total loss, not the value left.
b.clue: Find the total loss, then subtract it from the start.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out ($60 a year and $18 000 after 4 years), and the explanations match the card.
